prompt.context_jp: 「僕と鷹野___入社して もうすぐ半年になる」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「僕と鷹野___入社して もうすぐ半年になる」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that best fits Hiwada's reflective narration about reaching the six-month mark.

feedback.correct_en: This is a time-anchored event ('it's been almost six months since we joined'). The subordinate clause reports a new fact, so が marks the subject naturally.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would turn '僕と鷹野' into a topic contrasted with others, which doesn't fit this quiet opening reflection. を doesn't work grammatically here with 入社する.

contrast_examples.jp: 僕が入社して半年になる。
contrast_examples.en: It's been half a year since I joined.

contrast_examples.jp: 僕は、入社したのが半年前です。
contrast_examples.en: As for me, it was half a year ago that I joined.

prompt.context_jp: 「私 最近まで やってたよ」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「えっ 鷹野___？」
prompt.prompt_en: Hiwada reacts in surprise that it was TAKANO, of all people, who was trading stocks.

feedback.correct_en: Hiwada is incredulously identifying Takano as the (surprising) one doing it — exhaustive/identifying が, meaning 'YOU were doing it?'
feedback.incorrect_en: 鷹野は would just make her a general topic ('as for Takano...') and lose the shocked identification nuance. に is ungrammatical as a bare response here.

contrast_examples.en: Takano was the one doing it?
As for Takano, she wasn't doing it.

prompt.context_jp: 「ホチキスすら 留められなかった鷹野___ あんなに立派になって…」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「ホチキスすら 留められなかった鷹野___ あんなに立派になって…」
prompt.prompt_en: Hiwada is marveling that THIS Takano — the one who couldn't even staple — has grown so capable.

feedback.correct_en: The long relative clause describes a specific Takano; が presents her as the surprising subject of 'has become so impressive.' It's exclamatory new-info が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would frame her as an already-established topic and flatten the admiring exclamation. に doesn't fit the sentence structure.

contrast_examples.jp: あの子が立派になった。
あの子は立派になった。
contrast_examples.en: As for that kid, she's grown up.

prompt.context_jp: 並木の下で立ち止まって──
prompt.prompt_jp: 「僕 この会社___ なんとかやっていけそうです」
prompt.prompt_en: Hiwada reflects that he can manage at THIS company.

feedback.correct_en: やっていく takes で to mark the location/environment one gets by in. 'この会社で' = 'at this company.'
feedback.incorrect_en: が would wrongly make 会社 the subject of やっていく. を doesn't fit the intransitive 'manage/get by' meaning.

contrast_examples.jp: この会社でやっていける。
contrast_examples.en: I can make it work at this company.

prompt.context_jp: 「ウチの営業部___ 閉鎖することになった」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「ウチの営業部___ 閉鎖することになった」
prompt.prompt_en: The department head announces, as his topic of concern, that OUR sales department is being closed.

feedback.correct_en: The boss is setting '営業部' as the topic — 'As for our sales department, (the decision is that) it's being closed.' Formal announcement topic は.
feedback.incorrect_en: 営業部が makes it sound like just one new fact among many; it loses the heavy, topical weight of the announcement. を doesn't fit here.

contrast_examples.en: The sales dept. will be closed. (as topic)

contrast_examples.jp: 営業部が閉鎖される会社もある。
contrast_examples.en: There are also companies where sales depts get closed.

prompt.context_jp: 「ツミコ･タカノ氏___ 信頼できます」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「天才グローバル･フューチャー･ デザイン･コンサルタント… ツミコ･タカノ氏___ 信頼できます」
prompt.prompt_en: The speaker is pitching that Tsumiko Takano, specifically, is trustworthy.

feedback.correct_en: なら frames her as 'if it's her, then (we can trust)' — the conditional endorsement that fits the sales pitch.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would just mark her as subject but drops the 'if anyone, it's her' nuance. を doesn't work with 信頼できる (potential form).

contrast_examples.en: If it's him, you can trust him.

prompt.context_jp: 「もう シカゴで クライアント___待ってるよ」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「もう シカゴで クライアント___待ってるよ」
prompt.prompt_en: Hiwada tells Takano urgently that a client is waiting.

feedback.correct_en: 'There's a client waiting' — introducing a new, pressing fact. New-information が is the natural choice.
feedback.incorrect_en: クライアントは would presuppose the client as a known topic, but Hiwada is urgently announcing their existence/presence.

contrast_examples.jp: お客さんは三時に来ます。
contrast_examples.en: As for the customer, they'll come at 3.

prompt.context_jp: 「今 話しかけないで！ 自分___やって！」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「今 話しかけないで！ 自分___やって！」
prompt.prompt_en: The irritated developer snaps that Hiwada should do it himself.

feedback.correct_en: 自分で = 'by yourself / on your own' — で marks means/method.
feedback.incorrect_en: 自分を would literally mean 'do yourself' (as object). 自分が would mark the self as subject but sounds unnatural as a snapped command.

prompt.context_jp: 「全ロ計画代表の… 六角___ です」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「鷹野さん お久しぶりです 全ロ計画代表の… 六角___ です」
prompt.prompt_en: A stranger introduces himself formally.

feedback.correct_en: In '名前です' self-introductions, no particle appears between the name and です. The name is the predicate noun of an implicit topic (私は).
feedback.incorrect_en: 六角がです is ungrammatical; 六角を is not possible before です.

prompt.context_jp: 「取り柄___… 特にありません」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「取り柄___… 特にありません」
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle that gives '取り柄' a contrastive-topic feel ('as for selling points, there aren't any').

feedback.correct_en: は picks up '取り柄' from the previous question and marks it as topic/contrast: 'As for selling points, there aren't really any.' Classic は with a negative predicate.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would awkwardly re-introduce 取り柄 as new info, which is wrong since Rokkaku is responding to the previous question. を is ungrammatical with ありません.

contrast_examples.jp: 取り柄は特にありません。
contrast_examples.en: As for strong points, there really aren't any.

prompt.context_jp: 「なんだ 見かけ倒し___よ」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「なんだ 見かけ倒し___よ」
prompt.prompt_en: Hiwada mutters disappointedly that the robot is all show, no substance.

feedback.correct_en: なんだ…かよ is a set exasperated pattern meaning 'what, it's just X?!' The か-よ combination carries the disappointment.
feedback.incorrect_en: が and は would need a predicate after them; they don't produce the exclamatory 'oh, so it was just X!' tone.

contrast_examples.en: What — it was just a joke?

prompt.context_jp: 「鷹ロボのコンサル料として 2億___ 振り込まれたぞ！」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「2億___ 振り込まれたぞ！」
prompt.prompt_en: The boss shouts out the shocking amount that just hit the account.

feedback.correct_en: The 200 million yen is brand-new, astonishing information — classic が for existential/new-information subject.
feedback.incorrect_en: 2億は would presuppose it as known topic, flattening the shock. で doesn't fit with 振り込まれた.

contrast_examples.en: 200 million is a lot of money.

prompt.context_jp: 「鷹野の才能を最初に見抜いたの___ 俺だよ」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「鷹野の才能を最初に見抜いたの___ 俺だよ」
prompt.prompt_en: The boss insists HE was the one who first saw Takano's talent.

feedback.correct_en: The '〜のは Xだ' cleft is the natural pattern for 'The one who did Y was X.' は sets the clause as topic; 俺 gets the identifying focus.
feedback.incorrect_en: 〜のが俺だよ is awkward here; 〜のは俺だ is the standard cleft for this emphatic self-crediting. を doesn't fit.

contrast_examples.en: The one who saw through it was me.

prompt.context_jp: 「海外転職なんて 鷹野には壁___高すぎるよ」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「海外転職なんて 鷹野には壁___高すぎるよ」
prompt.prompt_en: Hiwada argues the hurdle is too high for Takano.

feedback.correct_en: With adjective predicates like 高い, the thing being described typically takes が: '壁が高い' = 'the wall is high.'
feedback.incorrect_en: 壁は would set 'wall' as topic, which is possible, but after a に-marked experiencer (鷹野には), が is the natural subject marker for the state.

contrast_examples.en: A wall is a tall structure. (defining topic)

prompt.context_jp: 「株って やったことある？」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「あっ 興味___ あるけど やったことはない」
prompt.prompt_en: Fill the blank so the sentence means 'I'm interested but have never done it.'

feedback.correct_en: は creates the contrast with the following 'but haven't done it': 'Interest, I have; but experience, no.' This mirror-structure with は…は is natural.
feedback.incorrect_en: 興味がある is grammatical in isolation, but here Hiwada is explicitly contrasting with やったことはない, so は is required to set up the parallelism.

contrast_examples.jp: 興味はあるけど、時間はない。
contrast_examples.en: I'm interested but I don't have time.

prompt.context_jp: 「ようやく ___に立つように なってきましたねえ」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「ようやく ___に立つように なってきましたねえ」
prompt.prompt_en: Fill the blank for 'they've finally started to be useful.'

feedback.correct_en: 役に立つ ('to be of use / useful') is the fixed idiom. 役 = 'role/use.'
feedback.incorrect_en: 腕に立つ and 手に立つ aren't standard expressions. 腕が立つ exists ('skilled'), but the pattern here is 〜に立つ, which requires 役.

prompt.context_jp: ノックして会議室に入りながら──
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the set phrase said when entering a meeting room.

feedback.correct_en: 失礼します is the standard business set phrase for 'excuse me (for entering/intruding).'
feedback.incorrect_en: 失敗します ('I'll fail') and 失望します ('I'll be disappointed') are not greetings and would be bizarre at a door.

prompt.context_jp: 「鶸田 鷹野 ___聞いてくれ」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「鶸田 鷹野 ___聞いてくれ」
prompt.prompt_en: The boss prefaces the bad news: 'Listen calmly.'

feedback.correct_en: 落ち着いて聞く = 'listen calmly' is the natural collocation when preparing someone for hard news.
feedback.incorrect_en: 立ち上がって (stand up) and 振り返って (look back) have the wrong semantics for the moment.

contrast_examples.jp: 立ち上がって挨拶した。
contrast_examples.en: He stood up and greeted them.

prompt.context_jp: 「イノベーションは ___な反応から始まるものです」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「イノベーションは ___な反応から始まるものです」
prompt.prompt_en: Rokkaku claims innovation always begins with THIS kind of reaction.

feedback.correct_en: 否定的な反応 = 'negative reaction' — the whole punchline is that people reject innovation at first.
feedback.incorrect_en: 積極的 (positive/proactive) is the opposite. 具体的 (concrete) doesn't match 'reaction' here.

prompt.context_jp: 送別の挨拶で──
prompt.prompt_jp: 「長い間 ___ になりました」
prompt.prompt_en: Takano's farewell set phrase: 'Thank you for taking care of me all this time.'

feedback.correct_en: お世話になりました is THE standard farewell/thank-you phrase in business.
feedback.incorrect_en: ご苦労になりました isn't a phrase. ご迷惑になりました would mean 'I've been a bother,' which is self-apology, not a general farewell.

contrast_examples.jp: ご迷惑をおかけしました。
contrast_examples.en: Sorry for the trouble I caused.

prompt.context_jp: 「高すぎるかは… ___ないと 分からないんじゃない？」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「高すぎるかは… ___ないと 分からないんじゃない？」
prompt.prompt_en: Takano's wisdom: you can't know if the wall is too high until you try to…

feedback.correct_en: 登ってみる ('try climbing') matches the 壁が高い metaphor Hiwada just used — you climb a wall to see if it's too tall.
feedback.incorrect_en: 倒してみる (knock down) and 壊してみる (break) are too aggressive and lose the 'try and see' nuance of 登ってみる.

contrast_examples.jp: やってみないと分からない。
contrast_examples.en: You won't know unless you try.

prompt.context_jp: 「本当は ただ… 少し ___ のかも」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「本当は ただ… 少し ___ のかも」
prompt.prompt_en: Hiwada finally admits what he's really feeling about Takano leaving.

feedback.correct_en: 寂しい ('lonely/sad to see her go') fits the realization: he's not jealous — he just doesn't want her to leave.
feedback.incorrect_en: 羨ましい (envious) is what he thought he felt but just rejected. 悔しい (frustrated/resentful) is also what he denied.

contrast_examples.jp: 友達が引っ越して寂しい。
彼が成功して羨ましい。

prompt.context_jp: 話を切り上げて次の商談に向かう場面──
prompt.prompt_jp: どちらが自然な、くだけた切り上げ方？
prompt.prompt_en: Which sounds more natural as a casual 'nevermind, let's go'?

choices.text: あっ もういいや 商談行くよ
あっ まだ良いのです 商談に行きますよ

feedback.correct_en: もういいや is a casual sentence-final expression meaning 'ah, forget it / nevermind.' Combined with 行くよ, it matches Takano's familiar tone with her peer.
feedback.incorrect_en: まだ良いのです is stiff, formal, and doesn't mean 'nevermind' — it would sound robotic and wrong for a coworker exchange.

contrast_examples.en: Ah, forget it, let's go home.
That's quite enough, thank you. (polite refusal)

prompt.context_jp: クライアントが真顔で言う──
prompt.prompt_jp: ビジネス場面で自然な言い回しは？
prompt.prompt_en: Which is the more natural business-polite rebuke?

choices.text: ジョークは やめてください それが あなたの仕事でしょう
ジョークを ストップしてください それが あなたの働きでしょう

feedback.correct_en: やめてください is the natural polite 'please stop,' and 仕事 is the correct word for 'job.' Option B uses English-loan ストップ awkwardly and 働き means 'labor/action,' not 'job role.'
feedback.incorrect_en: ストップしてください is understandable but stilted in business. 働き in this slot sounds odd — 仕事 is the right collocation.

contrast_examples.jp: 冗談はやめてください。
それがあなたの仕事です。

prompt.context_jp: 商談相手を見送る場面で──
prompt.prompt_jp: より自然なビジネスのお礼は？
prompt.prompt_en: Which is the more natural business-polite thank-you?

choices.text: ご多忙な中 ありがとうございました
忙しい時に ありがとうでした

feedback.correct_en: ご多忙な中 is the standard polite formula for 'thank you for taking time out of your busy schedule.' ありがとうございました is the correct past-polite form.
feedback.incorrect_en: ありがとうでした is not a natural past form; 忙しい時に lacks the honorific ご- expected in business.

contrast_examples.jp: お忙しい中、ありがとうございました。
contrast_examples.en: Thank you for your time, despite your busy schedule.

contrast_examples.jp: ありがとうございました。

prompt.context_jp: パスポートが要らないと言う鷹野に──
prompt.prompt_jp: どちらが自然な、呆れた指摘？
prompt.prompt_en: Which sounds more natural as Hiwada's exasperated 'of course not'?

choices.text: そんなわけないでしょう あしたにでも取りに行かないと
そんな理由ないでしょう あしたでも取りに行かなきゃ

feedback.correct_en: そんなわけない(でしょう) = 'there's no way that's the case' is the natural idiomatic expression. あしたにでも adds the urgency 'as early as tomorrow.'
feedback.incorrect_en: そんな理由ない means 'there's no such reason,' which doesn't fit the context — Hiwada isn't denying a reason but denying a mistaken belief.

prompt.context_jp: 同僚同士の雑談──
prompt.prompt_jp: 同僚への質問として、より自然なのは？
prompt.prompt_en: Which sounds more natural between coworkers of equal rank?

choices.text: 鶸田くん 株って やったことある？
鶸田くんは 株を やりましたことはございますか？

feedback.correct_en: The casual やったことある? with topic-marking って matches peer-to-peer office chat. 'Have you ever done stocks?'
feedback.incorrect_en: やりましたことはございますか is grammatically off (ある is nominal, not past-polite) and absurdly over-polite between desk neighbors.

contrast_examples.jp: 行ったことがありますか。
